Noisy gradients + sparse features (4 pts) (a) Learn in g-rate adap tatio n Momentum SGD: Single global α for all parameters. Adam: Per-parameter rates via α/(√^vt + ε). Large-gradient parameters get smaller rates; small-gradient parameters get larger rates. (b) Behavio r o n n o isy/sp arse data Noisy gradients: Adam's ^vt tracks variance — high noise increases ^vt, automatically shrinking step size. Momentum SGD has no such mechanism. Prevents division by zero when ^vt ≈ 0 Caps maximum step size at α/ε for parameters with tiny gradient history Sparse features: Rarely-updated parameters have small ^vt, giving them larger ef fective learning rates when gradients do arrive. This helps sparse features (e.g., word embeddings) learn quickly .
